newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac consults French PM, parliament leaders.
newsitem.headline: Chirac consults French PM, parliament leaders.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will consult Prime Minister Alain Juppe and the leaders of both houses of parliament on Monday, his office announced, amid mounting expectations that he will call a snap general election.

The consultations are required by the constitution before the president can dissolve the National Assembly to call a snap general election. Radio stations said Chirac had booked 10 minutes' broadcasting time on Monday night to make a statement.

The president's office has steadfastly refused comment on early election speculation, but cabinet ministers interviewed on Sunday night and Monday all spoke on the assumption that the decision was already certain and an announcement imminent.
The president's office said Chirac would meet Juppe, Senate president Rene Monory and National Assembly president Philippe Seguin separately beginning at 9.45 a.m. (0745 GMT).

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told Europe 1 radio that there were economic advantages to bringing forward the election due next March, since investment decisions were being delayed because of political uncertainty.

A SOFRES institute opinion poll published by the daily Le Figaro on Monday suggested the ruling centre-right coalition, which controls 478 of the Assembly's 577 seats, would lose up to 150 seats but keep an overall majority.
